title: 科学范式之演变
text: 科学进步究竟是知识的线性累积，还是认知框架的剧烈更迭？这一问题触及了科学哲学核心。托马斯·库恩在其著作中提出了范式概念。所谓范式，是指特定时期内科学共同体所共享的信念、理论及方法论。它为研究者提供了统一的观察视角。在常规科学阶段，学者们致力于在既有体系内解决具体问题。此时，绝大多数异常现象会被视为测量误差或个别偏差。然而，当反例积累到临界点，理论危机随之产生。这种矛盾会导致信任崩塌，从而引发科学革命。革命并非简单的逻辑推演，而是一种心理层面的整体转换。新旧范式之间存在着不可通约性。这意味着两种截然不同的世界观无法通过单一标准进行客观比较。例如，地心说与日心说的交替并非仅凭数据。它涉及对宇宙秩序之根本定义的重新构建。这种断裂式的跃迁改变了人类获取真理的路径。实证主义者倾向于认为真理是渐进逼近的。但库恩的观点强调了社会心理因素的影响。范式的更替决定了何为合法之研究课题。它界定了科学与伪科学的边界。这种权力结构塑造了学术话语体系。因此，科学演进并非单纯的客观真理揭示过程。它更像是一场关于认知主权的权力移交。理解这一机制有助于我们审视当代科研之局限。任何坚固的理论体系都可能在未来被颠覆。这种不确定性恰恰构成了科学探索的魅力所在。

questions.prompt: Who proposed the concept of 'paradigm' discussed in the text?
options: Thomas Kuhn
Karl Popper
Albert Einstein
Isaac Newton

questions.prompt: According to the text, what typically happens to anomalies during the 'normal science' stage?
options: They are usually dismissed as measurement error or individual deviation
They immediately trigger a scientific revolution
They are always found to disprove the entire paradigm
They are ignored because scientists refuse to record them

questions.prompt: What does 'incommensurability' between paradigms mean, according to the text?
options: Old and new paradigms represent worldviews that cannot be objectively compared using a single standard
Old and new paradigms are always numerically measurable against each other
New paradigms are always mathematically superior to old ones
It means two paradigms are identical in content

questions.prompt: How does the text characterize a scientific revolution, as opposed to gradual logical deduction?
options: As an overall transformation occurring at the psychological level
As a purely mathematical proof process
As an event with no relation to scientists' mindset
As something that never actually involves changing beliefs

questions.prompt: According to the text, what determines what counts as a legitimate scientific research topic?
options: The prevailing paradigm
Government funding priorities alone
Public opinion polls
The age of the researcher

patterns.title: 是…的
patterns.explanation: Used to emphasise when, where, how, or by whom a past action happened. The 是 introduces the emphasised element; 的 closes the structure.

patterns.title: 了 — completed action
patterns.explanation: Marks an action as completed (post-verbal 了) or a change of state (sentence-final 了). Worth re-reading whenever you spot it — the position shifts the meaning.

patterns.title: 被 passive
patterns.explanation: Marks the passive voice: the subject is acted upon. 被 introduces the agent (optional) and is followed by the verb.
